PullRequest.Title: agentHost: don't fail createSession when the sessions_v2 import registers its catalog first
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

## What

`createSession` could throw `Failed to register normalized chat catalog for <session>: conflict` even though the session was fine.

When a provider registers, the agent host runs a background `sessions_v2` import. If that import picks up a session that is still being created, it can record the session's verified catalog source between two steps of `_registerNewChatCatalog`:

1. the check "is there already a verified source or a catalog header?" (no, so continue), and
2. `registerChatCatalogV2`, whose transaction runs the same check again and now reports `conflict`.

`conflict` from `registerChatCatalogV2` means exactly what step 1 tests for, so it now gets the same outcome as step 1 (note the catalog as normalized and return) instead of failing session creation.

Found while making `agentService.test.ts` deterministic under CPU load (it surfaced once the chat-promotion tests stopped sharing one session database; see the follow-up PR). It can also happen for real users who create a session while that startup import is still running.

## How to test

New regression test: `createSession › creates a session whose chat catalog a concurrent synchronization recorded while it was being registered`. It stubs `registerChatCatalogV2` to return `conflict`. Without the fix it fails with the error above; with it, it passes.

- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts`: 1123 passing, 16 pending
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts`: 1123 passing, 16 pending
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: clean
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a normal non-provisional agent session when no concurrent catalog import wins the race
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider session creation completes first, then _registerNewChatCatalog synchronously reads the central catalog, checks sessions_v2, registers one catalog transaction, and notes normalized authority before SessionReady. The changed status predicate does not alter the applied/replayed/alreadyNormalized paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read one selected catalog snapshot and, if absent, one sessions_v2 record from the orchestrator SQLite database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one snapshot read and one keyed sessions_v2 read per newly created non-ephemeral session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same keyed reads occurred before the predicate change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both reads must complete before catalog registration and SessionReady.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction that checks catalog availability/source/header and inserts the initial catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized transaction per newly created non-provisional session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical transaction and successful-result handling occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The transaction is awaited by createSession.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh a loaded legacy-authority state record, potentially flushing its mirror and reading central session state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one refresh for the created session, and zero when the record is absent or already non-legacy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All ordinary successful registration statuses already reached this same refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When required, the refresh is awaited before creation continues.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One catalog registration per newly created non-provisional session; the candidate contains only the default chat, so work does not scale with historical session or chat count on this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each central database operation is serialized by AgentHostDatabase._transactionSequencer; session-state work is serialized per session. No concurrency, batching, or coalescing behavior changes in this scenario.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold or unloaded session-state record makes noteCatalogNormalized return immediately. A warm loaded legacy-authority record performs one refresh and changes to authority 2; there is no repeated miss or new retained cache entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate is reached after the existing transaction and is behaviorally identical for applied, replayed, and alreadyNormalized.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific creation latency and SQLite contention vary, but the diff changes none of those operations for ordinary successful creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the normal creation critical path, boundary count, cardinality, caching, and concurrency are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a session while background sessions_v2/catalog reconciliation records a verified source between the initial check and catalog registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The background migration runs off the creation path, but its central transaction races with createSession's registerChatCatalogV2 transaction. The transaction sequencer serializes them; when registration observes conflict, the changed branch now performs at most one authority refresh and allows creation to continue instead of throwing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Background reconciliation reads central catalog/session rows and may open session/chat databases to migrate metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded reconciliation batch with at most 4 sessions concurrently; per migrating session, chat metadata reads are limited to 4 concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same startup migration and bounded concurrency could race with creation before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Migration is background work, but its central transaction can briefly precede the serialized createSession registration transaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run one serialized registration transaction that sees the verified sessions_v2 source or catalog header and returns conflict.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction for the raced newly created session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same transaction returned conflict and createSession threw.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The transaction is awaited by createSession; the diff does not add or retry it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On the newly accepted conflict result, inspect the session-state cache and, only for a loaded legacy-authority record, read the normalized catalog, flush pending legacy mirror state, and read central state once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero operations for a cold/unloaded or already-normalized cache; otherwise one coalesced per-session refresh for this raced creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Conflict threw immediately, so no authority refresh ran and the user received no successfully created session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The refresh is awaited before successful createSession completion; previously this raced request terminated with an error instead of succeeding.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is bounded to the single newly created session whose registration overlaps migration; it does not fan out over all registered sessions. Background migration scale and limits are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog reconciliation admits up to 4 session migrations, while each migration's chat metadata work is limited to 4; all central SQLite transactions remain serialized. The session-state refresh uses a per-session sequencer. The diff adds no burst or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold/unloaded state makes the newly reached noteCatalogNormalized call a no-op. Warm legacy state incurs one authoritative refresh, then authority 2 suppresses future refreshes. Failed refreshes are recorded for the next locked load rather than retried in a loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the database implementation returns conflict only after observing an existing verified source/header in this registration method, and the changed line only admits that status to the existing normalized-authority refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The overlap frequency and warm-cache probability are uncertain, but the changed work is strictly bounded and replaces a failed user operation with a successful one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only new work is a single bounded cache-authority refresh required to complete a formerly failing raced creation; it introduces no repeated work, fan-out, retention, or concurrency burst.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced normal and raced session creation through the orchestrator SQLite transaction, startup catalog migration, session-state cache refresh, batching, and concurrency limits. The change only treats a serialized registration conflict as an already-recorded catalog and reaches the existing one-time authority refresh; no actionable performance regression or performance regression fix was identified.
